key_insight: TraceFEM enables spatial discretization of surface Stokes–Cahn–Hilliard dynamics with provable stability and error bounds under an exact-geometry assumption.
engineering_relevance: The analysis supports reliable simulation of coupled surface flow and phase separation on curved interfaces.
method: Use TraceFEM with stabilization that filters out Killing vector fields.
Establish inf-sup equivalence for trace Taylor–Hood pairs on two-dimensional surfaces.
Introduce p-dependent normal-derivative stabilization to derive approximation, inverse, and solution error estimates.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical analysis, including energy-norm error estimates and derived phase-variable bounds.
watch_item: The theory assumes no geometric error and treats spatial discretization only; geometry approximation and time stepping need separate assessment.
paper_title: Analysis of TraceFEM for the Surface Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard Model
